name: paper-finder-student-mcp
description: Academic paper search MCP server. Search scholarly papers, find open access copies and related work through OpenAlex (https://openalex.org), with no key needed. The tools listed below are the ones a client sees, and the old aliases still answer for saved prompts.

tools.name: search_papers
tools.description: Search scholarly papers by keywords. Returns title, authors, year, venue, citation count, DOI, a one line abstract and a free to read link when one exists. The results can be ordered, so you can get the most cited papers on a topic or the newest ones, and they can be limited to one kind of paper, to a range of years or to a minimum number of citations. Inputs: query (required keywords), from_year (optional earliest publication year), to_year (optional latest publication year), min_citations (optional, keep only the papers with at least this many citations), open_access_only (optional, false by default), type (optional, journal_article, preprint or book_chapter), sort (optional, relevance for the OpenAlex order, cited_by_count:desc for the most cited papers first, or publication_date:desc for the newest papers first), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'find the most cited papers on spaced repetition since 2020.'

tools.name: get_paper
tools.description: Details for one paper, including the abstract and a free to read link when one exists. A wrong or unknown reference returns a not found error that suggests searching by title or checking the DOI format. Inputs: paper (optional, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), doi (optional, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539 or a doi.org link, no OpenAlex ids). Give paper or doi, and paper wins if you give both. Example prompt: 'show me the abstract of DOI 10.1038/nature14539.'

tools.name: find_open_access_pdf
tools.description: Finds a free to read copy of one paper and returns the link, preferring a PDF over a landing page. When OpenAlex has no free copy it says so in plain words instead of failing. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807). Example prompt: 'find a free PDF of this paper, DOI 10.1038/nature14539.'

tools.name: find_related_papers
tools.description: Lists the papers that OpenAlex lists as related to a given paper, so you can find more work on the same topic. Every result carries a one line abstract, so you can judge a paper before you open it. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'what papers are related to DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762?'

tools.name: find_citing_papers
tools.description: Lists the papers that cite a given paper, newest first. Every result carries a one line abstract, so you can judge a paper before you open it. This is the other half of the citation graph that paper_references covers, so a literature review can walk the graph in both directions. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'who cited DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762?'

tools.name: paper_references
tools.description: The papers that one paper cites, which is the other half of the citation graph that find_citing_papers covers. Every result carries a one line abstract, so you can judge a paper before you open it. Use it to read the bibliography of a paper, to find the source a result came from, or to work backwards from a paper to the earlier work it builds on. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), sort (optional, cited_by_count:desc for the most cited references first, or publication_year:asc for the oldest references first), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'what papers does DOI 10.1038/nature14539 cite?'

tools.name: list_author_papers
tools.description: Papers by one author, most cited first. The name is looked up in the OpenAlex author records first, so initials, a different order of the name parts and other spellings of the same person still find the papers, and the papers are then taken from that author id. When OpenAlex has no record for the name, the papers are matched by the name as it is written on them. Inputs: author (required, the author name, for example Jane Doe, or an OpenAlex author id like A5108843829), from_year (optional earliest publication year), open_access_only (optional, false by default), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'list papers by John Dewey on education since 1950.'
